findings.problem: Four results, all from reading the code paths end to end (not executed against a live database). (1) Every additional browser adds a row with no from/to to the history, so the history shows changes that did not happen and loses the ones that did: a real change first seen by a browser with no saved copy is recorded without its direction. (2) The announcement can be lost for good: the workspace reaches 'Usable with founder support' on one computer (row with the change), the Dashboard is then opened anywhere without the saved copy (row with no change) or the state changes again, and Founding GTM, opened afterwards, finds a newest row that does not qualify. (3) It can also repeat: on a second browser the marker is missing, so if the qualifying row is still the newest the announcement shows again although it is described as once per workspace. (4) A write that fails (for example offline) is dropped on purpose (readiness-history.ts:158-166) after the saved copy of the state has already been advanced (lines 220-223), so that change is never recorded and can never be announced. Separately, the rule requires the change to end exactly at 'Usable with founder support' (ceremony.ts:69-73), so a workspace that goes from 'Partially documented' straight to a higher state — which is what both sample workspaces will do once the two reading defects are repaired — is never announced.
